sections.content: En cuanto (as soon as) links two events tightly in time -- the second happens immediately once the first does. With a past, completed event it takes the indicative; with something still pending or hypothetical, it takes the subjunctive. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: En cuanto anunció que Ecuador adoptaría el dólar estadounidense como moneda oficial, el presidente Jamil Mahuad desató una ola de protestas.
items.english: As soon as he announced that Ecuador would adopt the US dollar as its official currency, President Jamil Mahuad set off a wave of protests.

items.spanish: En cuanto los manifestantes indígenas tomaron el Congreso Nacional, se formó brevemente una junta de gobierno.
items.english: As soon as the indigenous protesters took over the National Congress, a governing junta briefly formed.

items.spanish: En cuanto la junta se disolvió esa misma madrugada, el poder pasó directamente al vicepresidente Gustavo Noboa.
items.english: As soon as the junta dissolved that very early morning, power passed directly to Vice President Gustavo Noboa.

items.spanish: En cuanto se estabilizó la situación bajo Noboa, Ecuador se convirtió en uno de los pocos países del mundo en adoptar por completo la moneda de otro país.
items.english: As soon as the situation stabilized under Noboa, Ecuador became one of the few countries in the world to fully adopt another country's currency.

sections.content: En cuanto is interchangeable with tan pronto como in most contexts. Don't confuse it with en cuanto a (as for, regarding), which introduces a topic rather than a time relationship.
